gates.wave_gate: Schema and data parity validated against the source database before cutover. Once replication to Aurora MySQL has caught up, decommission the source MySQL database: later waves move from Aurora MySQL, not from it. Close RISK-004 and RISK-005 before this gate (source objects' database logic and design trade-offs).

stacks.name: dms-replication
stacks.purpose: DMS replication instance, source and target endpoints, and the full-load and ongoing-replication task

cost_assumptions: One Multi-AZ DMS replication instance (dms.r6i.large, the stack's default MultiAZ=true) with 100 GB of allocated storage (100 GB included in the instance price, the rest billed per GB) runs the full load and ongoing replication for step 1

Instance size: 0.2998 GB and 190.986 writes per second: up to 500 GB and 1000 writes per second. Memory-optimized (16 GiB) so changes stay in memory up to 1,000 writes per second; 100 GB of storage holds task logs and changes that spill from memory during a full load of up to 500 GB (this catalog's choice).
The migration is billed as one month (730 hours); the instance is removed once the step cuts over
With MultiAZ=false the instance and its storage cost 128.48 USD per month
The targets' own cost is in the total cost of ownership, not repeated here
Prices: AWS Price List, us-east-1, on-demand, retrieved on 2026-11-04
notes: The lag gate is 30 seconds of capture lag, a default to tune against the lagging reads' tolerance
